old_digest: /root/ec-wip-fdp/digest.txt at 511 lines, as the live course was written from
new_digest: /root/ec-wip-fdp/digest.txt at 534 lines, rebuilt by ec6_dump.mjs, byte-reproducible and byte-identical under a second timezone

method.corpus: ALL 78 lessons (src/content/courses/fdp/**/*.md) and ALL 396 LIVE questions, the questions read out of the applied seed migrations 20260918_ec6_fdp_seed_{beginner,intermediate,advanced}.sql rather than out of the wave's bank JSONs, so the manifest describes what production actually serves.
method.moved_values: Every numeric literal the old teaching digest printed and the rebuilt digest does not, matched in its canonical four-decimal form AND in every rounded (0 to 3 dp) and comma-grouped restatement, each with a numeric boundary on both sides so a match is never a fragment of a longer number.
method.moved_referent: Three values the rebuilt digest still prints, but now labels as the case WITHOUT the end-of-life cost (2047.5653, 29.5998, 1048.6281). Quoting them as the plan's answer is false even though the literal survives.
method.falsified_claims: Six prose patterns with no moved number of their own, each paired with the digest line that settles it.
two_defects_found_in_this_sweep_and_fixe: An exact-literal sweep alone was checked against a rounded-restatement sweep. 0 of 404 value-hits turned out to be rounded-only, but the check had to be run: the corpus quotes the digest's canonical four-decimal forms. An earlier substring version of that check reported 32 false hits for '628' because 628 sits inside 0.628637, which is why every match here carries a numeric boundary.

The claim patterns first used [^.] as a sentence guard. A decimal point inside a number ends that window, so 'at 30.0000 USD a barrel gives -898.3507 and multiple-roots' was invisible to it and intermediate/m06/l03-onward.md was missed. The guard is now (?:[^.\n]|\.(?=\d)), which found 17 further claim instances and two further questions.
